keyTerms.definition: B/N + q: brute force wins below break-even N.
sum 1/(k+rank): ranks need no calibration across systems.
measured, derived, stated, opinion: in that order.

recall.question: Write the index amortization formula. When does brute force win?
recall.answer: Amortized = B/N + q. Brute force wins below break-even N.

recall.question: Write the RRF formula. Why do ranks beat raw scores?
recall.answer: RRF = sum 1/(k+rank). Ranks need no calibration across systems.

recall.question: Write the quality-gate rule.
recall.answer: Ship iff delta >= -epsilon on the task metric.

keyTerms.definition: One-time index cost vs marginal per-request cost.
B/(brute - q) = 160,000 on the toy.
Hourly news rebuilds reset the amortization.

recall.question: Deep ladder 1 prices a retrieval index: build 7200 s, query 5 ms, brute 50 ms. What are the amortized cost and break-even?

sections.title: Deep ladder 2: from retrieval to defense

keyTerms.definition: Staged funnel: ANN, filter, cross-encoder rerank.
The reranker: 400/405 of the cascade cost.
The assumption: an ANN recall miss means the reranker never sees the gold.

recall.question: Deep ladder 2 prices the retrieval cascade and the quality gate. What dominates, and what is the tightened cost?
recall.answer: 5 + 400 = 405 ms; the reranker is 400/405 of the cost. Top 10: 205 ms. Gate: ship iff delta >= -epsilon.

keyTerms.definition: Two mid ranks beat one top plus one deep rank.
What a sound table promotes a stated claim to.

recall.question: Fusion: doc D ranks (3, 5), doc E ranks (1, 100), k=60. Compute both RRF scores. Why does D win?
recall.answer: D: 0.031258. E: 0.022643. D wins because fusion rewards agreement across systems over one loud rank.

recall.question: Grade three claims: “2x faster” (no table), “O(T d^2)” (derivable), “SSMs are the future”. A table then appears for the first with sound baselines: new grade?
recall.answer: Stated, derived, opinion. With a sound table: measured. Still check: baselines current, seeds reported, metric ungameable.

keyTerms.definition: The gate matches the documented epsilon.

recall.question: D1. The gate below ships everything, including a candidate 2% worse. What is the bug, the fix, and the invariant?
recall.answer: Bug: epsilon is 5%, not 0.5% (0.05 vs 0.005). Fix: return delta >= -0.005. Invariant: the gate matches the documented epsilon.

keyTerms.definition: Indexes always win on latency; the choice becomes recall-vs-latency.
Gate on a held-out human eval or a metric family.
Lead with the gaming analysis.

recall.question: Rebuilds are free and instant. What happens to the index-vs-brute-force choice and the cascade design?
recall.answer: Indexes always win on latency (build cost zero): the choice becomes pure recall-vs-latency. Widen funnels freely (query latency still binds).

recall.question: The quality metric is perfectly gameable and everyone knows it. How do you redesign the gate and the defense?
recall.answer: Gate on a held-out human eval or a metric family (no single number). Defense: lead with the gaming analysis. The first question becomes “how did you prevent gaming.”

keyTerms.definition: Only semantic queries tested invalidates.
The retriever running 10x slower invalidates.

recall.question: A paper claims “our retriever beats BM25 on every query type.” What five audit questions do you ask?
recall.answer: (1) Query types? (2) BM25 tuned? (3) Latency matched? (4) Corpus? (5) Significance?
